english.title: Arson with intent to endanger life
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) committed arson in that without lawful excuse

(A)_[destroyed]_
(B)_[damaged]_

by fire **(..SPECIFY PROPERTY..)

(C)_[to the value of **(..SPECIFY VALUE..)]_
(D)_[of a value unknown]_

belonging to **(..SPECIFY PERSON..) intending to destroy or damage such property and intending by the said destruction or damage to endanger the life of **(..SPECIFY PERSON..)
english.legislation: Contrary to sections 1(2), 1(3) and 4 of the Criminal Damage Act 1971.
english.pointstoprove:
date and location
committed arson in that without lawful excuse
destroyed/damaged by fire property belonging to another
with intent to destroy/damage the property
and with intent by that destruction/damage to endanger life

investigatoraction.description: DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes:
This CJS Code and Standard Offence Wording document OBSOLETE from 31/12/11. New version at CJS Code CD71003 and H8111.

(i) With aggravated offence, recklessness as to whether life endangered must be charged separately - R v Hoof (1981). See H4372 for offence wording.
(ii) The consent of the Director of Public Prosecutions is required where the damage is to a spouse's property (section 30(4) of the Theft Act 1968).
(iii) Property damaged or destroyed may belong to defendant.
(iv) The same incident may involve separate activities, some causing ordinary damage and some damage by fire (for example, protestors break into a laboratory building, smash laboratory equipment and set fire to some files). In such circumstances they are separate offences and best charged as such (R v Booth 1999).
